supporting_observations.claim: At 13:42:46–13:42:47 UTC, WS-EBROOKS-01 made Kerberos and LDAP connections to 10.54.20.10, near the alerted account-creation time.

The supplied network evidence shows domain-service traffic from WS-EBROOKS-01, but does not establish that this traffic created svc_update or that the account-management action originated from this workstation.

known_telemetry_limitations: The provided records are network-flow, DNS, and proxy logs; they do not include domain-controller account-management audit events or equivalent evidence of the account creation.
The network records do not identify the initiating user or process for the Kerberos and LDAP connections, or reveal the LDAP operation performed.
The supplied evidence does not show whether svc_update was placed in a group, assigned privileges, or used after creation.
claims_not_established: Whether svc_update was actually created at the reported time and, if so, which user or process created it.
Whether the account creation was authorized, related to the scheduled svc-inventory password rotation, or malicious.
Whether svc_update received privileges or was used for subsequent activity.
additional_evidence_needed: Obtain DC-BLU-01 account-management audit events around 13:42 UTC, including the creator, target account, and any group or privilege changes.
Review relevant identity and endpoint logs from the account-creation source, including process and command-line telemetry if available.
Check change records or administrator/help-desk confirmation for svc_update and determine whether it was associated with the svc-inventory rotation.
